title: Cut Nodes Out and List the Remaining Trees

concept.title: A node is a new root when its parent was deleted and it was not
body: If some nodes are deleted from a tree, what is left is usually several separate trees, a *forest*. Every **surviving node whose parent was deleted** (or the original root, if it survives) becomes the **root** of one of the trees in the forest. Print all these trees.

A single recursion over the tree can do it. The function receives the node and a flag "is the parent deleted (or is there no parent)?". It decides whether the node itself is deleted; if it is **not deleted but its parent was**, it is a new root, and it is added to the list. Then both children are processed with the flag "my deletion state", and the child links are updated: a deleted child is replaced by "nothing".

body.code:
def prune(node, is_root):               # is_root: no parent, or the parent was deleted
    if node is None:
        return None
    deleted = node.val in gone
    if is_root and not deleted:
        roots.append(node)              # a new tree starts here
    node.left = prune(node.left, deleted)
    node.right = prune(node.right, deleted)
    return None if deleted else node    # the parent forgets a deleted child

body: The roots are collected in the order in which the recursion meets them, which is the **pre-order** of the original tree. A set of the values to delete makes each test O(1). After the recursion, each root in the list is the root of a finished tree, because the links to the deleted nodes were cut on the way.

statement: A binary tree with different values and a list of values are given. Delete the nodes with these values; every remaining node whose parent was deleted becomes the root of a separate tree (and the original root stays a root if it is not deleted). Print the remaining trees, one per line, each in level order in the same form as a tree in the input (`N` for a missing child, no `N` at the end). The trees are ordered by the position of their roots in the pre-order of the original tree. If no node remains, print `empty`.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
The third line has `d`, the number of values to delete.
The fourth line has the `d` values to delete.
outputFormat: One line for every remaining tree, or `empty`.
constraints: -10^9 <= every value <= 10^9, and all values are different
The height of the tree is at most 800.
1 <= d <= number of nodes; the values to delete are different and are in the tree.

examples.note: Deleting 3 and 5 leaves the trees 1 2 N 4 (the root 1 with the child 2 whose child is 4), 6 and 7.

hints: Put the values to delete into a set.
Recurse with a flag that tells whether the parent was deleted; a surviving node with such a parent is a new root.
Return nothing for a deleted node so that its parent drops the link; print the roots in the order they were found.

explanation: A recursion with the flag "the parent was deleted or does not exist" adds every surviving node with such a parent to the list of roots, and returns nothing for a deleted node so that its parent drops the link.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root


# Prints a tree in the same level-order form ("empty" for no tree).
def print_tree(root):
    if root is None:
        print("empty")
        return
    out = []
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    while head < len(queue):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if node is None:
            out.append("N")
        else:
            out.append(str(node.val))
            queue.append(node.left)
            queue.append(node.right)
    while out and out[-1] == "N":
        out.pop()
    print(" ".join(out))


def delete_nodes(root, to_delete):
    gone = set(to_delete)
    roots = []

    def prune(node, is_root):
        if node is None:
            return None
        deleted = node.val in gone
        if is_root and not deleted:
            roots.append(node)
        node.left = prune(node.left, deleted)
        node.right = prune(node.right, deleted)
        return None if deleted else node

    prune(root, True)
    return roots

gone = list(map(int, input().split()))

roots = delete_nodes(build_tree(vals), gone)
